newsitem.title: UK: Precious metals tumble, led by palladium sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Precious metals tumble, led by palladium sell-off.

text.p: A sudden speculative onslaught swept precious metals prices sharply lower on Monday, with palladium and platinum suffering the biggest losses.
Gold prices, already vulnerable after crumbling in late trading on Monday, slid to a fresh low of $345.30 an ounce, down nearly $5 from Monday's London close.
Prices then bounced slightly to fix at $346.30 an ounce, compared to $347.40 in the morning.
"If the selling pressure from the funds eases off, we could see a bounce from the very good physical offtake we've been seeing in gold and silver," a London-based dealer said.
"But so far there's no sign of that happening."
A measure of support was expected to emerge between $343.50 and $345.00, technical analysts said. Further down, gold's mid-February low of $336.15 remained a key level.
Silver was also weaker at $5.15/$5.17, a decline of seven cents from Monday's close. Support around $5.10 was expected to prove solid should the market head lower.
But palladium, followed closely by platinum, caught the biggest blow in what dealers said was an unexpected move in the already nervous market.
Palladium was indicated at $142.25/$143.25, a decline of $9.50 from Monday's London close.
"There's nothing fundamental that I can see to warrant this sell off," a senior dealer said.
"It's likely a technical move in a thin market, with not a lot of buying around."
Another dealer noted: "There's no obvious catalyst for the funds to start selling right now."
However, the market was wary that the move could be a precursor to fresh news news that negotiators for key producer Russia were opening long-delayed 1997 contract talks with importer Japan.
"A sharp movement will be a forerunner of an announcement that talks or shipments have started," a dealer had cautioned before the sell-off.
Platinum prices were similarly weaker at $371.00/$372.00 an ounce, a drop of $8.25.
Although platinum followed palladium lower, it had been vulnerable to the downside following gold's slide on Monday, dealers said.
"Platinum had held pretty well after gold lost ground and it probably felt it needed to play catch-up," a dealer said.
